variable {E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace E]

theorem actual_density_test_transfer_from_low_likelihood_region
    (base : Measure E) (p q h : E → ℝ) (S : Set E) (hS : MeasurableSet S)
    (hp : Integrable p base) (hq : Integrable q base)
    (hhp : Integrable (fun z => h z * p z) base)
    (hhq : Integrable (fun z => h z * q z) base)
    (hh : ∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1)
    (cutoff : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ cutoff)
    (hinside : ∀ z ∈ S, q z ≤ cutoff * p z)
    (houtside : ∀ z ∉ S, cutoff * p z ≤ q z)
    (hmass : (∫ z in S, p z ∂base) ≤ ∫ z, h z * p z ∂base) :
    (∫ z in S, q z ∂base) ≤ ∫ z, h z * q z ∂base := by
  have hpoint (z : E) :
      cutoff * (h z * p z - S.indicator p z) ≤ h z * q z - S.indicator q z := by
    by_cases hz : z ∈ S
    · simp only [Set.indicator_of_mem hz]
      have hn : 0 ≤ (1-h z) * (cutoff*p z-q z) :=
        mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr (hh z).2) (sub_nonneg.mpr (hinside z hz))
      nlinarith
    · simp only [Set.indicator_of_notMem hz, sub_zero]
      have hn := mul_nonneg ((hh z).1) (sub_nonneg.mpr (houtside z hz))
      nlinarith
  have hi := integral_mono ((hhp.sub (hp.indicator hS)).const_mul cutoff)
    (hhq.sub (hq.indicator hS)) hpoint
  simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at hi
  rw [integral_const_mul,integral_sub hhp (hp.indicator hS),
    integral_sub hhq (hq.indicator hS),integral_indicator hS,integral_indicator hS] at hi
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg ht (sub_nonneg.mpr hmass)]

theorem actual_density_test_transfer_from_high_likelihood_region
    (base : Measure E) (p q h : E → ℝ) (S : Set E) (hS : MeasurableSet S)
    (hp : Integrable p base) (hq : Integrable q base)
    (hhp : Integrable (fun z => h z * p z) base)
    (hhq : Integrable (fun z => h z * q z) base)
    (hh : ∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1)
    (cutoff : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ cutoff)
    (hinside : ∀ z ∈ S, cutoff * p z ≤ q z)
    (houtside : ∀ z ∉ S, q z ≤ cutoff * p z)
    (hmass : (∫ z, h z * p z ∂base) ≤ ∫ z in S, p z ∂base) :
    (∫ z, h z * q z ∂base) ≤ ∫ z in S, q z ∂base := by
  have hpoint (z : E) :
      h z * q z - S.indicator q z ≤ cutoff * (h z * p z - S.indicator p z) := by
    by_cases hz : z ∈ S
    · simp only [Set.indicator_of_mem hz]
      have hn : 0 ≤ (1-h z) * (q z-cutoff*p z) :=
        mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr (hh z).2) (sub_nonneg.mpr (hinside z hz))
      nlinarith
    · simp only [Set.indicator_of_notMem hz, sub_zero]
      have hn := mul_nonneg ((hh z).1) (sub_nonneg.mpr (houtside z hz))
      nlinarith
  have hi := integral_mono (hhq.sub (hq.indicator hS))
    ((hhp.sub (hp.indicator hS)).const_mul cutoff) hpoint
  simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at hi
  rw [integral_const_mul,integral_sub hhp (hp.indicator hS),
    integral_sub hhq (hq.indicator hS),integral_indicator hS,integral_indicator hS] at hi
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg ht (sub_nonneg.mpr hmass)]

theorem actual_bounded_measurable_test_has_integrable_density_products
    (base : Measure E) (p h : E → ℝ) (hp : Integrable p base)
    (hm : Measurable h) (hh : ∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1) :
    Integrable (fun z => h z * p z) base := by
  apply hp.bdd_mul hm.aestronglyMeasurable
  exact ae_of_all base (fun z => by
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs,abs_of_nonneg (hh z).1]
    exact (hh z).2)


open CompleteAppliedGaussianCDF CompleteAppliedGaussianQuantile

theorem actual_scalar_shifted_gaussian_density_ratio (shift point : ℝ) :
    gaussianPDFReal shift 1 point = gaussianPDFReal 0 1 point *
      Real.exp (shift*point-shift^2/2) := by
  simp only [gaussianPDFReal,NNReal.coe_one,mul_one,sub_zero]
  rw [mul_assoc, ← Real.exp_add]
  congr 2
  ring

theorem actual_scalar_gaussian_low_halfspace_is_a_likelihood_region
    (shift threshold : ℝ) (hshift : 0 ≤ shift) :
    (∀ point ≤ threshold, gaussianPDFReal shift 1 point ≤
      Real.exp (shift*threshold-shift^2/2) * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 point) ∧
    (∀ point ≥ threshold, Real.exp (shift*threshold-shift^2/2) *
      gaussianPDFReal 0 1 point ≤ gaussianPDFReal shift 1 point) := by
  constructor <;> intro point hp
  · rw [actual_scalar_shifted_gaussian_density_ratio shift point]
    rw [mul_comm (Real.exp _)]
    apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (gaussianPDFReal_nonneg _ _ _)
    exact Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by nlinarith)
  · rw [actual_scalar_shifted_gaussian_density_ratio shift point]
    rw [mul_comm (Real.exp _)]
    apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (gaussianPDFReal_nonneg _ _ _)
    exact Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by nlinarith)

theorem actual_shifted_scalar_gaussian_halfspace_mass (shift threshold : ℝ) :
    (gaussianReal shift 1).real (Iic threshold) = standardCDF (threshold-shift) := by
  have hmap : (gaussianReal 0 1).map (fun x : ℝ => x+shift) = gaussianReal shift 1 := by
    simpa using (gaussianReal_map_add_const (μ:=0) (v:=1) shift)
  have hh := map_measureReal_apply (μ:=gaussianReal 0 1)
    (show Measurable (fun x : ℝ => x+shift) by fun_prop) (s:=Iic threshold) measurableSet_Iic
  rw [hmap] at hh
  have hs : (fun x : ℝ => x+shift) ⁻¹' Iic threshold = Iic (threshold-shift) := by
    ext x
    simp only [mem_preimage,mem_Iic]
    constructor <;> intro hx <;> linarith
  simpa only [hs,standardCDF] using hh

theorem actual_scalar_gaussian_transfer_for_every_bounded_measurable_test
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hm : Measurable h) (hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1)
    (shift threshold : ℝ) (hshift : 0 ≤ shift)
    (hbase : standardCDF threshold ≤ ∫ z, h z ∂gaussianReal 0 1) :
    standardCDF (threshold-shift) ≤ ∫ z, h z ∂gaussianReal shift 1 := by
  have hp := integrable_gaussianPDFReal 0 1
  have hq := integrable_gaussianPDFReal shift 1
  have hhp := actual_bounded_measurable_test_has_integrable_density_products volume _ h hp hm hb
  have hhq := actual_bounded_measurable_test_has_integrable_density_products volume _ h hq hm hb
  have hi := actual_scalar_gaussian_low_halfspace_is_a_likelihood_region shift threshold hshift
  have hx (mean : ℝ) : (gaussianReal mean 1).real (Iic threshold) =
      ∫ z in Iic threshold, gaussianPDFReal mean 1 z := by
    rw [measureReal_def,gaussianReal_apply_eq_integral _ (by norm_num),ENNReal.toReal_ofReal]
    exact integral_nonneg (fun z => gaussianPDFReal_nonneg _ _ _)
  have hf (mean : ℝ) : (∫ z, h z ∂gaussianReal mean 1) =
      ∫ z, h z * gaussianPDFReal mean 1 z := by
    rw [integral_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul (by norm_num : (1:ℝ≥0)≠0)]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul,mul_comm]
  have hbase' : (∫ z in Iic threshold, gaussianPDFReal 0 1 z) ≤
      ∫ z, h z * gaussianPDFReal 0 1 z := by
    rw [←hx 0,←hf 0]
    exact hbase
  have ht := actual_density_test_transfer_from_low_likelihood_region volume
    (gaussianPDFReal 0 1) (gaussianPDFReal shift 1) h (Iic threshold)
    measurableSet_Iic hp hq hhp hhq hb (Real.exp (shift*threshold-shift^2/2))
    (Real.exp_pos _).le (fun z hz => hi.1 z hz)
    (fun z hz => hi.2 z (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hz))) hbase'
  rw [←hx shift,actual_shifted_scalar_gaussian_halfspace_mass,←hf shift] at ht
  exact ht

theorem actual_scalar_ideal_majority_for_every_strict_standardized_shift
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hm : Measurable h) (hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1)
    (shift : ℝ) (hshift : 0 ≤ shift) (hradius : shift < 2)
    (hbase : standardCDF 2 ≤ ∫ z, h z ∂gaussianReal 0 1) :
    (1/2:ℝ) < ∫ z, h z ∂gaussianReal shift 1 := by
  have htransfer := actual_scalar_gaussian_transfer_for_every_bounded_measurable_test
    h hm hb shift 2 hshift hbase
  have hhalf : (1/2:ℝ) < standardCDF (2-shift) := by
    rw [←actual_standard_gaussian_symmetry_and_half_mass]
    apply actual_standard_gaussian_cdf_is_continuous_and_strictly_increasing.2
    linarith
  exact hhalf.trans_le htransfer


variable {Y : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Y] [MeasurableSingletonClass Y]

def scalarClassMass (classifier : ℝ → Y) (shift : ℝ) (label : Y) : ℝ :=
  (gaussianReal shift 1).real (classifier ⁻¹' {label})

def scalarIdealWinner (classifier : ℝ → Y) (shift : ℝ) (label : Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ other, other ≠ label → scalarClassMass classifier shift other < scalarClassMass classifier shift label

theorem actual_scalar_ideal_classifier_retains_every_true_majority_label
    (classifier : ℝ → Y) (hf : Measurable classifier) (label : Y)
    (shift : ℝ) (hshift : 0 ≤ shift) (hradius : shift < 2)
    (hbase : standardCDF 2 ≤ scalarClassMass classifier 0 label) :
    scalarIdealWinner classifier shift label := by
  let A := classifier ⁻¹' {label}
  have hA : MeasurableSet A := hf (measurableSet_singleton label)
  let h : ℝ → ℝ := A.indicator (fun _ => 1)
  have hm : Measurable h := measurable_const.indicator hA
  have hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1 := by
    intro z
    by_cases hz : z ∈ A <;> simp [h,hz]
  have hh (mean : ℝ) : (∫ z, h z ∂gaussianReal mean 1) = scalarClassMass classifier mean label := by
    simpa only [h,scalarClassMass,A,smul_eq_mul,mul_one] using
      (integral_indicator_const (μ:=gaussianReal mean 1) (1:ℝ) hA)
  have hmj : (1/2:ℝ) < scalarClassMass classifier shift label := by
    rw [←hh shift]
    exact actual_scalar_ideal_majority_for_every_strict_standardized_shift h hm hb shift hshift hradius
      (by rw [hh 0]; exact hbase)
  intro other hother
  let B := classifier ⁻¹' {other}
  have hB : MeasurableSet B := hf (measurableSet_singleton other)
  have hd : Disjoint A B := by
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    intro z ha hb
    exact hother (hb.symm.trans ha)
  have hu := measureReal_mono (μ:=gaussianReal shift 1)
    (s₁:=A∪B) (s₂:=univ) (subset_univ _)
  rw [measureReal_union hd hB] at hu
  have hone : (gaussianReal shift 1).real univ = 1 := by simp
  rw [hone] at hu
  change scalarClassMass classifier shift label + scalarClassMass classifier shift other ≤ 1 at hu
  linarith

theorem actual_scalar_confidence_is_over_estimation_samples
    {Omega : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Omega]
    (samples : Measure Omega) [IsProbabilityMeasure samples]
    (classifier : ℝ → Y) (hf : Measurable classifier) (selectedLabel : Omega → Y)
    (confidenceEvent : Set Omega) (hconfidence : (999/1000:ℝ) ≤ samples.real confidenceEvent)
    (hvalid : ∀ omega ∈ confidenceEvent,
      standardCDF 2 ≤ scalarClassMass classifier 0 (selectedLabel omega)) :
    (999/1000:ℝ) ≤ samples.real {omega | ∀ shift : ℝ,
      0 ≤ shift → shift < 2 → scalarIdealWinner classifier shift (selectedLabel omega)} := by
  apply hconfidence.trans
  apply measureReal_mono (h₂:=by finiteness)
  intro omega homega shift hnonnegative hstrict
  exact actual_scalar_ideal_classifier_retains_every_true_majority_label classifier hf
    (selectedLabel omega) shift hnonnegative hstrict (hvalid omega homega)

theorem actual_scalar_boundary_halfspace_has_no_strict_majority :
    (gaussianReal 2 1).real (Iic 2) = 1/2 ∧
    (gaussianReal 2 1).real (Iic 2)ᶜ = 1/2 ∧
    ¬ ((gaussianReal 2 1).real (Iic 2)ᶜ < (gaussianReal 2 1).real (Iic 2)) := by
  have hh : (gaussianReal 2 1).real (Iic 2) = 1/2 := by
    rw [actual_shifted_scalar_gaussian_halfspace_mass]
    norm_num only [sub_self]
    exact actual_standard_gaussian_symmetry_and_half_mass
  have hc := measureReal_add_measureReal_compl (μ:=gaussianReal 2 1)
    (s:=Iic 2) measurableSet_Iic
  rw [hh] at hc
  have hone : (gaussianReal 2 1).real univ = 1 := by simp
  rw [hone] at hc
  refine ⟨hh, by linarith, ?_⟩
  rw [hh]
  linarith

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

def orthogonalResidual (unit : E) : E →L[ℝ] E :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E - (innerSL ℝ unit).smulRight unit

theorem actual_standard_gaussian_unit_projection_law (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) :
    (stdGaussian E).map (fun z : E => ⟪unit,z⟫) = gaussianReal 0 1 := by
  have hg := (IsGaussian.hasGaussianLaw_id (μ:=stdGaussian E)).map_fun (innerSL ℝ unit)
  have hv : Var[fun z : E => ⟪unit,z⟫; stdGaussian E] = 1 := by
    have ht := variance_dual_stdGaussian (innerSL ℝ unit)
    simpa only [coe_innerSL_apply,innerSL_apply_norm,hu,one_pow] using ht
  have hg' : HasGaussianLaw (fun z : E => ⟪unit,z⟫) (stdGaussian E) := by
    simpa only [id_eq,innerSL_apply_apply] using hg
  rw [hg'.map_eq_gaussianReal]
  have hm : (∫ z : E, ⟪unit,z⟫ ∂stdGaussian E) = 0 := by
    simpa only [coe_innerSL_apply] using integral_strongDual_stdGaussian (innerSL ℝ unit)
  rw [hm,hv]
  norm_num

theorem actual_gaussian_projection_and_orthogonal_residual_are_independent
    (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) :
    IndepFun (fun z : E => ⟪unit,z⟫) (orthogonalResidual unit) (stdGaussian E) := by
  have hg := IsGaussian.hasGaussianLaw_id (μ:=stdGaussian E)
  have hpair := hg.map_fun ((innerSL ℝ unit).prod (orthogonalResidual unit))
  have hc (a b : E) : cov[fun z : E => ⟪a,z⟫,fun z : E => ⟪b,z⟫; stdGaussian E] = ⟪a,b⟫ := by
    rw [←covarianceBilin_apply_eq_cov IsGaussian.memLp_two_id,
      covarianceBilin_stdGaussian,innerSL_apply_apply]
  have hnorm : ⟪unit,unit⟫ = 1 := by rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq,hu];norm_num
  have hpair' : HasGaussianLaw (fun z : E => (⟪unit,z⟫,orthogonalResidual unit z)) (stdGaussian E) := by
    simpa only [id_eq,ContinuousLinearMap.prod_apply,innerSL_apply_apply] using hpair
  apply hpair'.indepFun_of_covariance_inner
  intro scalar vector
  have hi (v : E) : MemLp (fun z : E => ⟪v,z⟫) 2 (stdGaussian E) := by
    simpa only [id_eq,innerSL_apply_apply] using (hg.map_fun (innerSL ℝ v)).memLp_two
  have hr (a b : ℝ) : ⟪a,b⟫ = a*b := by
    simp only [RCLike.inner_apply,conj_trivial,mul_comm]
  simp only [hr,orthogonalResidual,sub_apply,ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply,
    ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply,innerSL_apply_apply]
  change cov[fun z : E => scalar * ⟪unit,z⟫,
    fun z : E => ⟪vector,z-⟪unit,z⟫ • unit⟫; stdGaussian E] = 0
  simp only [inner_sub_right,real_inner_smul_right]
  rw [covariance_const_mul_left,covariance_fun_sub_right (hi unit) (hi vector)
    ((hi unit).mul_const ⟪vector,unit⟫),covariance_mul_const_right,hc,hc,hnorm]
  rw [real_inner_comm unit vector]
  ring

theorem actual_full_gaussian_joint_noise_decomposition (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) :
    (stdGaussian E).map (fun z : E => (⟪unit,z⟫,orthogonalResidual unit z)) =
      (gaussianReal 0 1).prod ((stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit)) ∧
    (∀ z : E, ⟪unit,z⟫ • unit + orthogonalResidual unit z = z) := by
  have hi := actual_gaussian_projection_and_orthogonal_residual_are_independent unit hu
  have hj := hi.map_prod_eq_prod_map_map (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
  rw [actual_standard_gaussian_unit_projection_law unit hu] at hj
  refine ⟨hj,?_⟩
  intro z
  simp only [orthogonalResidual,ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply,ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply,
    ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply,innerSL_apply_apply]
  abel


theorem actual_bounded_probability_test_integrable
    {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (measure : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure measure]
    (f : X → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (hb : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) :
    Integrable f measure := by
  have hp : Integrable (fun _ : X => (1:ℝ)) measure := integrable_const 1
  have hh := hp.bdd_mul hf.aestronglyMeasurable (ae_of_all measure (fun x => by
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs,abs_of_nonneg (hb x).1]
    exact (hb x).2))
  simpa only [mul_one] using hh

theorem actual_bounded_gaussian_fiber_integral_decomposition
    (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) (f : E → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ f z ∧ f z ≤ 1) :
    Measurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v)
      ∂((stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit))) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ (∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v)
      ∂((stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit))) ∧
      (∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v)
        ∂((stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit))) ≤ 1) ∧
    (∫ z : E, f z ∂stdGaussian E) =
      ∫ t : ℝ, (∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v)
        ∂((stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit))) ∂gaussianReal 0 1 := by
  let residualLaw := (stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit)
  let F : ℝ × E → ℝ := fun p => f (p.1 • unit + p.2)
  have hF : Measurable F := hf.comp (by fun_prop)
  have hFb : ∀ p, 0 ≤ F p ∧ F p ≤ 1 := fun p => hb _
  have hi := actual_bounded_probability_test_integrable
    ((gaussianReal 0 1).prod residualLaw) F hF hFb
  have hm : Measurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v) ∂residualLaw) :=
    hF.stronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'.measurable
  refine ⟨hm,?_,?_⟩
  · intro t
    have hft : Measurable (fun v : E => f (t • unit + v)) := hf.comp (by fun_prop)
    have hit := actual_bounded_probability_test_integrable residualLaw _ hft (fun v => hb _)
    refine ⟨integral_nonneg (fun v => (hb _).1),?_⟩
    have hx := integral_mono hit (integrable_const (1:ℝ)) (fun v => (hb _).2)
    simpa using hx
  · have hj := actual_full_gaussian_joint_noise_decomposition unit hu
    calc
      (∫ z : E, f z ∂stdGaussian E) =
          ∫ z : E, F (⟪unit,z⟫,orthogonalResidual unit z) ∂stdGaussian E := by
        apply integral_congr_ae
        exact ae_of_all _ (fun z => by change f z=f (⟪unit,z⟫ • unit + orthogonalResidual unit z);rw [hj.2 z])
      _ = ∫ p : ℝ × E, F p ∂((stdGaussian E).map
          (fun z : E => (⟪unit,z⟫,orthogonalResidual unit z))) :=
        (integral_map_of_stronglyMeasurable (by fun_prop) hF.stronglyMeasurable).symm
      _ = ∫ p : ℝ × E, F p ∂((gaussianReal 0 1).prod residualLaw) := by rw [hj.1]
      _ = ∫ t : ℝ, (∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v) ∂residualLaw) ∂gaussianReal 0 1 :=
        integral_prod F hi


theorem actual_shifted_gaussian_fiber_integral
    (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) (f : E → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ f z ∧ f z ≤ 1) (shift : ℝ) :
    (∫ z : E, f (shift • unit + z) ∂stdGaussian E) =
      ∫ t : ℝ, (∫ v : E, f (t • unit + v)
        ∂((stdGaussian E).map (orthogonalResidual unit))) ∂gaussianReal shift 1 := by
  have hg : Measurable (fun z : E => f (shift • unit + z)) := hf.comp (by fun_prop)
  have hd := actual_bounded_gaussian_fiber_integral_decomposition unit hu
    (fun z : E => f (shift • unit + z)) hg (fun z => hb _)
  have hm := (actual_bounded_gaussian_fiber_integral_decomposition unit hu f hf hb).1
  have hmap : (gaussianReal 0 1).map (fun t : ℝ => t+shift) = gaussianReal shift 1 := by
    simpa using (gaussianReal_map_add_const (μ:=0) (v:=1) shift)
  have hi := integral_map_of_stronglyMeasurable (μ:=gaussianReal 0 1)
    (show Measurable (fun t : ℝ => t+shift) by fun_prop) hm.stronglyMeasurable
  rw [hmap] at hi
  rw [hd.2.2,hi]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  exact ae_of_all _ (fun t => by
    apply integral_congr_ae
    exact ae_of_all _ (fun v => by
      congr 1
      rw [add_smul]
      abel))

theorem actual_nd_gaussian_event_transfer_for_every_bounded_measurable_test
    (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) (f : E → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ f z ∧ f z ≤ 1) (shift threshold : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ shift)
    (hbase : standardCDF threshold ≤ ∫ z : E, f z ∂stdGaussian E) :
    standardCDF (threshold-shift) ≤ ∫ z : E, f (shift • unit+z) ∂stdGaussian E := by
  have hd := actual_bounded_gaussian_fiber_integral_decomposition unit hu f hf hb

  apply actual_scalar_gaussian_transfer_for_every_bounded_measurable_test
    _ hd.1 hd.2.1 shift threshold hs
  rw [←hd.2.2]
  exact hbase

theorem actual_nd_true_majority_inside_every_strict_direction
    (unit : E) (hu : ‖unit‖ = 1) (f : E → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)

    (hball : ‖perturbation‖ < 2*sigma)
    (hbase : standardCDF 2 ≤ ∫ z : E, f (location+sigma • z) ∂stdGaussian E) :
    (1/2:ℝ) < ∫ z : E, f (location+perturbation+sigma • z) ∂stdGaussian E := by

    apply integral_congr_ae

      change f (location+perturbation+sigma • z)=f (location+sigma • (sigma⁻¹ • perturbation+z))
      rw [smul_add,smul_smul,mul_inv_cancel₀ (ne_of_gt hsigma),one_smul]

    have hh : (1/2:ℝ) < standardCDF 2 := by

      apply actual_standard_gaussian_cdf_is_continuous_and_strictly_increasing.2

  let f : E → ℝ := A.indicator (fun _ => 1)
  have hf : Measurable f := measurable_const.indicator hA
  have hb : ∀ z, 0 ≤ f z ∧ f z ≤ 1 := by
    intro z

  have hmajor : (1/2:ℝ) < ndClassMass classifier (location+perturbation) sigma label := by
    have hm := actual_scaled_nd_gaussian_majority_for_every_strict_euclidean_ball
      f hf hb location perturbation sigma hsigma hball
      (by rw [actual_nd_class_mass_is_the_genuine_gaussian_indicator_integral classifier hc];exact hbase)
    rw [actual_nd_class_mass_is_the_genuine_gaussian_indicator_integral classifier hc] at hm
    exact hm

  let U : Set E := (fun z : E => classifier (location+perturbation+sigma • z)) ⁻¹' {label}
  let V : Set E := (fun z : E => classifier (location+perturbation+sigma • z)) ⁻¹' {other}

    intro z hu hv

  rw [measureReal_union hd hV] at hsum

entire_local_section_definition_theorem_:
Sections 2–3 certify a network by looking inside it. Randomized smoothing certifies a different classifier, built from any base classifier by averaging over Gaussian noise, and never looks inside at all. That is what lets it reach ImageNet scale. In this section $\sigma$ is the noise level, $\delta$ is an adversarial perturbation and $\alpha$ is the failure probability of the Monte-Carlo certificate.

Definition — Smoothed classifier (Cohen, Rosenfeld & Kolter, 2019)
Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal Y$ be any measurable deterministic or random base classifier with a finite label set $\mathcal Y$ (internal randomness independent of the Gaussian draw and with a fixed law on every call), and $\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I)$ with $\sigma>0$ (see Primer C). The smoothed classifier returns the most probable class of $f$ under noise, $$ g(x) = \arg\max_{c\in\mathcal Y}\ \mathbb P\big(f(x+\varepsilon)=c\big). $$ Write $p_A=\mathbb P(f(x+\varepsilon)=c_A)$ for the top class and $p_B$ for the runner-up.
Theorem — Certified ℓ2 radius (Cohen et al., Theorem 1) and its tightness (Theorem 2)
Suppose that for a given $x$ there are $c_A\in\mathcal Y$ and $\underline{p_A},\overline{p_B}\in[0,1]$ with $$ \mathbb P\big(f(x+\varepsilon)=c_A\big)\ \ge\ \underline{p_A}\ \ge\ \overline{p_B}\ \ge\ \max_{c\ne c_A}\mathbb P\big(f(x+\varepsilon)=c\big). $$ Then $g(x+\delta)=c_A$ for all $\|\delta\|_2\lt R$, where $$ R = \frac{\sigma}{2}\Big(\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})-\Phi^{-1}(\overline{p_B})\Big), $$ $\Phi^{-1}$ the standard Gaussian quantile function. The displayed finite formula assumes $0\lt\overline{p_B}\le\underline{p_A}\lt1$; endpoint bounds use limits. If the loose bounds are both $1$, the difference is indeterminate: $\underline{p_A}=1$ implies all competitors have probability zero, so use the tighter valid bound $\overline{p_B}=0$, giving an infinite radius. The radius is tight: if $\underline{p_A}+\overline{p_B}\le 1$, and the $K=|\mathcal Y|$ labels leave room for the remaining probability, $\underline{p_A}+(K-1)\,\overline{p_B}\ge 1$, then for every $\|\delta\|_2\gt R$ there is a base classifier consistent with the class probabilities for which $g(x+\delta)\ne c_A$. (Cohen et al. state only the first condition. Without the second, normalisation forces $\mathbb P(f(x+\varepsilon)=c_A)\ge 1-(K-1)\overline{p_B}\gt\underline{p_A}$, and a larger radius follows.)

In words. Beyond measurability and a fixed randomisation law, nothing is assumed about $f$; only the two numbers $\underline{p_A}$, $\overline{p_B}$ matter. The radius grows with $\sigma$ (more smoothing), with $\underline{p_A}$ and with the gap to $\overline{p_B}$; it is $\ell_2$ specifically, because the Gaussian is rotation-invariant. Tightness means that the theorem cannot be improved without assuming more about $f$. The proof is a hypothesis-testing argument: the worst-case base classifier is a half-space perpendicular to $\delta$.

Proof — Theorem 1 via the Neyman–Pearson lemma

Lemma (Neyman–Pearson, Cohen et al. Lemma 3). Let $X,Y$ have densities $\mu_X,\mu_Y$ on $\mathbb R^d$ and let $h:\mathbb R^d\to\{0,1\}$ be any (possibly random) test. If $S=\{z:\mu_Y(z)\le t\mu_X(z)\}$ for some $t\gt 0$ and $\mathbb P(h(X)=1)\ge\mathbb P(X\in S)$, then $\mathbb P(h(Y)=1)\ge\mathbb P(Y\in S)$. (Part 2: with $\ge t$ and $\le$, the conclusion is $\le$.)

Proof of the lemma. Write $h(1|z)$ for the probability that $h(z)=1$ and $S^c$ for the complement. Then

$$ \begin{aligned} \mathbb P(h(Y)=1)-\mathbb P(Y\in S) &= \int_{S^c}h(1|z)\mu_Y\,dz-\int_S h(0|z)\mu_Y\,dz\\ &\ge t\Big[\int_{S^c}h(1|z)\mu_X\,dz-\int_S h(0|z)\mu_X\,dz\Big]\\ &= t\big[\mathbb P(h(X)=1)-\mathbb P(X\in S)\big]\ \ge\ 0 . \end{aligned} $$

The first equality splits $\int h(1|z)\mu_Y$ over $S$ and $S^c$ and uses $h(1|z)=1-h(0|z)$ on $S$; the inequality uses $\mu_Y\ge t\mu_X$ on $S^c$ and $\mu_Y\le t\mu_X$ on $S$ (both with the right sign because of the minus in front of the second integral); the last equality reverses the first step for $X$. $\square$

Specialisation to Gaussians (Lemma 4). For $X\sim\mathcal N(x,\sigma^2I)$ and $Y\sim\mathcal N(x+\delta,\sigma^2I)$,

$$ \frac{\mu_Y(z)}{\mu_X(z)} = \exp\!\Big(\frac{-\|z-x-\delta\|^2+\|z-x\|^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big) = \exp\!\Big(\frac{2\delta^{\top}(z-x)-\|\delta\|^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big), $$

a strictly increasing function of $\delta^{\top}z$. Hence every half-space $\{\delta^{\top}z\le\kappa\}$ is a likelihood-ratio set $\{\mu_Y/\mu_X\le t\}$ (and $\{\delta^{\top}z\ge\kappa\}$ one of the form $\{\mu_Y/\mu_X\ge t\}$), so the lemma applies to half-spaces normal to $\delta$.

Main argument. Fix $\delta\ne0$ (for $\delta=0$, $R\gt0$ means $\underline{p_A}\gt\overline{p_B}$, which already makes $c_A$ the unique top class) and a competitor class $c_B\ne c_A$; put $X=x+\varepsilon$, $Y=x+\delta+\varepsilon$. Take $0\lt\overline{p_B}\le\underline{p_A}\lt1$, so that all quantiles below are finite; a bound equal to $0$ or $1$ can be replaced by a valid bound arbitrarily close to it, which gives the theorem with $\Phi^{-1}(0)=-\infty$, $\Phi^{-1}(1)=+\infty$ (only $\underline{p_A}=\overline{p_B}\in\{0,1\}$ is indeterminate). We must show $\mathbb P(f(Y)=c_A)\gt\mathbb P(f(Y)=c_B)$. Define the half-spaces

$$ A=\{z:\ \delta^{\top}(z-x)\le\sigma\|\delta\|\,\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})\},\qquad B=\{z:\ \delta^{\top}(z-x)\ge\sigma\|\delta\|\,\Phi^{-1}(1-\overline{p_B})\}. $$

Step 1: $A$ and $B$ match the known probabilities under $X$. Since $\delta^{\top}(X-x)=\delta^{\top}\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2\|\delta\|^2)$, the variable $\delta^{\top}(X-x)/(\sigma\|\delta\|)$ is standard normal, so $\mathbb P(X\in A)=\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A}))=\underline{p_A}$ and $\mathbb P(X\in B)=1-\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(1-\overline{p_B}))=\overline{p_B}$.

Step 2: apply the lemma twice. With $h=\mathbf 1[f(\cdot)=c_A]$ we have $\mathbb P(h(X)=1)\ge\underline{p_A}=\mathbb P(X\in A)$, so $\mathbb P(f(Y)=c_A)\ge\mathbb P(Y\in A)$. With $h=\mathbf 1[f(\cdot)=c_B]$ and part 2 of the lemma, $\mathbb P(h(X)=1)\le\overline{p_B}=\mathbb P(X\in B)$ gives $\mathbb P(f(Y)=c_B)\le\mathbb P(Y\in B)$.

Step 3: compute the two probabilities under $Y$. Now $\delta^{\top}(Y-x)=\|\delta\|^2+\delta^{\top}\varepsilon$, so

$$ \mathbb P(Y\in A)=\Phi\Big(\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})-\frac{\|\delta\|}{\sigma}\Big),\qquad \mathbb P(Y\in B)=\Phi\Big(\Phi^{-1}(\overline{p_B})+\frac{\|\delta\|}{\sigma}\Big), $$

using $-\Phi^{-1}(1-p)=\Phi^{-1}(p)$ for the second. Step 4. Because $\Phi$ is increasing, $\mathbb P(Y\in A)\gt\mathbb P(Y\in B)$ if and only if $\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})-\|\delta\|/\sigma\gt\Phi^{-1}(\overline{p_B})+\|\delta\|/\sigma$, i.e. $\|\delta\|\lt\tfrac\sigma2(\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})-\Phi^{-1}(\overline{p_B}))=R$. Chaining Steps 2–4 gives $\mathbb P(f(Y)=c_A)\ge\mathbb P(Y\in A)\gt\mathbb P(Y\in B)\ge\mathbb P(f(Y)=c_B)$ for every $c_B$, hence $g(x+\delta)=c_A$. $\square$

Tightness (Theorem 2). The base classifier $f^\star$ that returns $c_A$ on $A$, $c_B$ on $B$ and other classes elsewhere is well defined when $\underline{p_A}+\overline{p_B}\le1$ (the hypothesis of Theorem 2): then $\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})\le\Phi^{-1}(1-\overline{p_B})$, so $A$ and $B$ are disjoint except, at equality, for their common boundary hyperplane, which has probability zero under every Gaussian and can be given to either class. It is consistent with the class probabilities (Step 1) provided the leftover mass $1-\underline{p_A}-\overline{p_B}$ can be shared among the other $K-2$ classes with at most $\overline{p_B}$ each, i.e. $\underline{p_A}+(K-1)\overline{p_B}\ge1$. The paper leaves this implicit; it holds automatically for CERTIFY’s choice $\overline{p_B}=1-\underline{p_A}$. It can fail: with two classes, $\underline{p_A}=0.6$ and $\overline{p_B}=0.3$ give $R\approx0.389\sigma$, yet normalisation forces $p_A\ge0.7$, which certifies $0.524\sigma$. When the condition holds, Step 3 shows that $f^\star$ has $\mathbb P(f^\star(Y)=c_A)\lt\mathbb P(f^\star(Y)=c_B)$ for every $\|\delta\|\gt R$: the half-space is the worst case, and the bound cannot be improved.

Connection to Module 13 — smoothing is a Lipschitz certificate in disguise
A more general statement published shortly afterwards by Levine et al. and Salman et al. (2019) is quoted in footnote 2 of Cohen et al. (Salman et al., NeurIPS 2019, Lemma 2, stated there for $\sigma=1$): if $h:\mathbb R^d\to[0,1]$ is measurable and $\hat h(x)=\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[h(x+\varepsilon)]$, then $x\mapsto\Phi^{-1}(\hat h(x))$ is $1/\sigma$-Lipschitz. The probit score is finite whenever $h$ is neither $0$ nor $1$ almost everywhere, because the Gaussian density is positive everywhere and so $0\lt\hat h\lt1$; if $h$ is $0$ or $1$ almost everywhere, $\hat h$ is constant. Its probit score is then infinite rather than a real Lipschitz function, so these endpoint cases are excluded from the finite-score theorem; robustness of the constant probability is immediate. (Proof: the Neyman–Pearson argument above, run with the $[0,1]$-valued test $h$ and a half-space of probability $\hat h(x)$, gives $\hat h(x+\delta)\ge\Phi\big(\Phi^{-1}(\hat h(x))-\|\delta\|_2/\sigma\big)$; apply the increasing $\Phi^{-1}$, then exchange $x$ and $x+\delta$.) Applying it to $h=\mathbf 1[f(\cdot)=c_A]$ and to $h=\mathbf 1[f(\cdot)=c_B]$ for every $c_B\ne c_A$, each probit score moves by at most $\|\delta\|_2/\sigma$, so their gap, at least $\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})-\Phi^{-1}(\overline{p_B})$ at $x$, shrinks by at most $2\|\delta\|_2/\sigma$ and stays positive for $\|\delta\|_2\lt R$: Theorem 1 again. So randomized smoothing is a Lipschitz-margin certificate for the transformed scores $\Phi^{-1}(p_c)$, exactly the margin-over-Lipschitz logic of Module 13, with the Lipschitz constant guaranteed by the noise instead of by the architecture.

Monte-Carlo certification and its price

$p_A$ cannot be computed exactly for a neural base classifier, so it is estimated, and the certificate becomes a statistical statement.

Algorithm 2: CERTIFY (Cohen et al.)
  1. Draw $n_0$ noisy copies $x+\varepsilon_i$, evaluate $f$, and let $\hat c_A$ be the most frequent class. // selection sample, $n_0=100$ in the paper
  2. Draw $n$ fresh noisy copies and count $k=\#\{i: f(x+\varepsilon_i)=\hat c_A\}$. // estimation sample, $n=100{,}000$
  3. $\underline{p_A}\leftarrow$ one-sided Clopper–Pearson lower confidence bound (see Primer C) at level $1-\alpha$ for a Binomial$(n,p)$ parameter given $k$ successes. // $\alpha=0.001$
  4. If $\underline{p_A}\gt\tfrac12$: return $\hat c_A$ with radius $R=\sigma\,\Phi^{-1}(\underline{p_A})$; else ABSTAIN. // uses $\overline{p_B}:=1-\underline{p_A}$ in Theorem 1

The two samples are kept separate for a statistical reason. Conditional on the selection sample, $\hat c_A$ is a fixed label, and each of the $n$ fresh draws votes for it independently with the same probability $p=\mathbb P(f(x+\varepsilon)=\hat c_A)$, so $k\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(n,p)$ and the Clopper–Pearson bound applies. Choosing the label and estimating its probability on the same draws would favour whichever label happened to do well on them, and the fixed-label interval would no longer be valid without a correction for that selection. With probability at least $1-\alpha$ over the sampling, a returned certificate is correct (Proposition 2 of the paper). Two costs follow. First, $10^5$ forward passes per certified input: 15 s per CIFAR-10 image (110-layer ResNet) and 110 s per ImageNet image (ResNet-50) on an RTX 2080 Ti. Second, the radius is capped by $n$: even if $f$ returns $c_A$ on all $n$ samples, the best lower bound is $\underline{p_A}=\alpha^{1/n}$, so $R\le\sigma\Phi^{-1}(\alpha^{1/n})$, which is $1.50\sigma$ for $n=100$, $3.20\sigma$ for $n=10^4$ and $3.81\sigma$ for $n=10^5$ at $\alpha=0.001$; certifying $4\sigma$ at 99.9% confidence has the sufficient sample count $n\ge\ln(10^3)/(1-\Phi(4))\approx2.2\times10^5$. Prediction alone is cheap (PREDICT: $n=100$ samples and a two-sided binomial test, 0.15 s).

Derivation — The sample count needed to certify a radius $r\sigma$

If all $n$ draws vote for $\hat c_A$, the one-sided Clopper–Pearson bound solves $\mathbb P(\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\ge n)=p^n=\alpha$, so $\underline{p_A}=\alpha^{1/n}$ and $R=\sigma\Phi^{-1}(\alpha^{1/n})$. Hence $R\ge r\sigma$ iff $\alpha^{1/n}\ge\Phi(r)$ iff $\ln\alpha\ge n\ln\Phi(r)$ iff $n\ge\ln(1/\alpha)/\big(-\ln\Phi(r)\big)$ (dividing by the negative number $\ln\Phi(r)$ flips the inequality). With $u=1-\Phi(r)$ we have $-\ln\Phi(r)=-\ln(1-u)=u+\tfrac{u^2}2+\dots\ge u$, so $n\ge\ln(1/\alpha)/u$ is sufficient, and almost exact for small $u$. For $r=4$, $\alpha=10^{-3}$: $u=3.17\times10^{-5}$, and both expressions give $n\approx2.18\times10^5$.

Denoised smoothing. Theorem 1 holds for any base classifier, so the base classifier may include a denoiser. Carlini et al., ICLR 2023 use an off-the-shelf diffusion model as a one-shot denoiser in front of an off-the-shelf classifier: the forward process $x_t=\sqrt{\alpha_t}\,x+\sqrt{1-\alpha_t}\,\mathcal N(0,I)$ is matched to the smoothing noise by choosing $t^\star$ with $\sigma^2=(1-\alpha_{t^\star})/\alpha_{t^\star}$ (their eq. 4; here $\alpha_t$ is the diffusion noise schedule, not a failure probability), and the rescaled noisy input $\sqrt{\alpha_{t^\star}}(x+\varepsilon)$, $\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I)$, is denoised in one step and classified. The matching is one line: with $\varepsilon=\sigma Z$, $Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I)$, the input is $\sqrt{\alpha_{t^\star}}\,x+\sqrt{\alpha_{t^\star}}\,\sigma Z$, and $\alpha_{t^\star}\sigma^2=1-\alpha_{t^\star}$ is exactly the choice of $t^\star$, so it has the law $\sqrt{\alpha_{t^\star}}\,x+\sqrt{1-\alpha_{t^\star}}\,Z$ of the diffusion inputs the denoiser was trained on. For the certificate the denoiser is simply part of the base classifier: the composition of the rescaling, the one-step denoiser at time $t^\star$ and the classifier is fixed during certification (any internal randomness has the same law on every call), so Theorem 1 applies to it unchanged; the quality of the denoising affects $p_A$ and hence the radius, never soundness. No training is needed, and the certified ImageNet top-1 accuracies are 71.1 / 54.3 / 38.1 / 29.5% at $\ell_2$ radii 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 (BEiT-L classifier, 552M-parameter diffusion model, $n=10^4$ samples). The best deterministic certificates are far behind at large radii: the 2B-parameter LipNeXt reaches 41.2% certified accuracy at radius $36/255\approx 0.14$ and 22.4% at radius 1 (Hu, Hu & Fredrikson, ICLR 2026; see Module 13).

Pitfall — the two certificates are not the same kind of statement
